reasoning_traces.think:
The reasoning spine \( \mathcal{R} = \text{reason}(\mathcal{I}) \) integrates all signal bundles \( \mathcal{I} \) into a single coherent score. This is achieved by applying a Bayesian update kernel that incorporates calibrated weights \( \mathcal{W}_{\text{slice}} \) to raw signals \( \mathcal{S} \). The resulting \( P_{\text{calib}}(W) \) becomes the input to \( \text{reason()} \). The decision genome \( \Delta \mathcal{G} \) then applies aperture logic to \( \mathcal{R} \) based on contextual constraints \( \mathcal{C} \), producing a decision state transition. Dualities arise in how \( \mathcal{I} \) is decomposed into \( \mathcal{S} \) and \( \mathcal{W}_{\text{slice}} \), and how \( \mathcal{R} \) is transformed into \( \Delta \mathcal{G} \). Failure modes include uncalibrated inputs, missing context, or invalid aperture logic.
